In criminal cases the charge must be proved beyond reasonable doubt,

So, also in civil cases there may be degrees of probability.

Agreeing, with this statement of law, Hodson, LJ said, Just as in civil cases the balance of probability may be more readily fitted in one case than in another, so in criminal cases proof beyond reasonable doubt may more readily be attained in some cases than in others.

sentences.text: Whether a civil or a criminal case, the anvil for testing of 'proved', 'disproved' and 'not proved', as defined in Section 3 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 is one and the same.

A fact is said to be 'proved' when, if considering the matters before it, the Court either believes it to exist, or considers its existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of a particular case, to act upon the supposition that it exists.
It is the evaluation of the result drawn by applicability of the rule, which makes the difference.

The probative effects of evidence in civil and criminal cases are not however always the same and it has been laid down that a fact may be regarded as proved for purposes of a civil suit, though the evidence may not be considered sufficient for a conviction in a criminal case.

opennyai_summary.facts:
It is further stated that defendant number 1 did not repay the CS No. 476308/2015 Raj Kumar Gupta Vs. Brij Mohan & Anr. Page No. 2 of 14 loan amount back as agreed within the stipulated period of seven months i.e. by 18.05.2014.
Thereafter, in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure, Indian Evidence Act, etc plaintiff led his piece of evidence.
On 22.01.2021, the Predecessor of this Hon'ble Court closed the defence evidence of defendants.
Further, due to prevailing circumstances of Covid-19, both defendant no.1 and his counsel lost track of the case.
opennyai_summary.issue:
(I) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for a decree of recovery of rupees 3,99,100/-
alongwith interest @ 24% per annum as prayed in the suit?
10. Now, coming to the issue wise findings, one specific issue which was culled out in the instant case was, whether the plaintiff is entitled for a decree of recovery of rupees 3,99,100/- alongwith interest @ CS No. 476308/2015 Raj Kumar Gupta Vs. Brij Mohan & Anr.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It shall not cause prejudice to plaintiff and if not allowed defendants shall be deprived of justice and suffer an irreparable loss,
harm and injury.
It is primarily to enable the court to clarify any issue or doubt by recalling any witness either suo motu or an application of any party so that the court can itself put questions and elicit answers.
It has also been held that the power under Section 151 CPC is not intended to be used routinely.
If so used, it will defeat the very purpose of various amendments to the Code to expedite trials.
But where the application is found to be bonafide and where the additional evidence, oral or documentary, will assist the Court to clarify the evidence on the issues and will assist in rendering justice, CS No.
476308/2015 Raj Kumar Gupta Vs. Brij Mohan & Anr. Page No. 8 of 14 the Court is satisfied that non production earlier was valid and sufficient reasons, the Court may exercise its discretion to recall the witnesses or permit the fresh evidence.
In such circumstances, the Court was left with no other option but to close the defendant's evidence vide order dated 22.01.2021.
It is needless to state that after dismissal of the application of defendant no.1 under Order XLI Rule 1 r/w Sec. 151CPC, filing of the present application under Section 151 CPC with the similar prayer for permission to cross examine PW-1 is not maintainable before this court.
It is on record that the conduct of defendants is very much evident from the record.
Hence, the Court is convinced that this is not a fit case where the court should exercise its discretionary power under section 151 CPC.
In view of the above, no ground is made out to allow the present application and hence the same is dismissed being devoid of any merit.
This position is found favourable in various judgments of Hon'ble Superior Courts and specially in Thiruvengada Pillai v. Navaneethammal & Anr., Writ Petition Raj Kumar Gupta vs Brij Mohan on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156933963/
6 (Civil) 290/2001, decided on 19.02.2008 and also in Shantilal Gulabchand Mutha v Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Limited 2013 4 SCC 396.
In witnesses whereof the parties of this agreement have set their respective hands on the date month and year first above given.
Defendants have also not disputed the execution of the present loan agreement.
Though the circumstances of its execution are disputed by the defendants.
Now, the situation is that both the plaintiff and defendants are on same line qua the execution of this particular loan agreement, except the way of its execution.
Also, it is observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in R.V.E. Venkatachala Gounder v. Arulmigu Viswesaraswami & V.P.
Temple & Anr, 2003 SCC Online SC 1117 that:
Now, in the totality of all these circumstances, explicitly the burden of proof which was lying upon the plaintiff to prove his contentions has been successfully discharged by him qua the remaining amount of rupees 1 lakh due towards the defendant number 1.
Though, any other amount claimed by the plantiff being interest for the period of nine months or the expenditure incurred on installing channel gate and paying of electricity bill was not proved as such, and loan agreement Ex.PW1/1 is also absolutely silent on that aspect.
Thus, after the evaluation of relevant piece of evidence led on behalf of plaintiff, plaintiff seems to be successful in shifting the onus upon the defendant number 1 by creating high degree of probability of liability of defendant number 1 of an amount of rupees 1 lakh.
opennyai_summary.decision:
3. The application may kindly be dismissed with heavy cost in the interest of justice.
The application is disposed off accordingly.
Defendant number 1 has miserably failed to discharge this onus and CS No. 476308/2015 Raj Kumar Gupta Vs. Brij Mohan & Anr. Page No. 13 of 14 is thus liable for an amount of rupees 1 lakh to be paid to plaintiff.
The plaintiff is also claiming the interest at the rate of 24% per annum in the present suit.
The said interest of rate, in my opinion, is excessive and exorbitant.
In view of prevailing economic situation,
the ends of justice shall be served in case the defendant is made to pay simple interest on the abovesaid sum at the rate of 6% per annum to the plaintiff.
12. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case coupled with evidence adduced on record by plaintiff, suit is decreed and plaintiff is held entitled to recover an amount of rupees 1,00,000/- (one lakhs) from defendant no. 1 alongwith simple interest on the said sum at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of present suit till its realization.
13. Parties to bear their own costs.
14. Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
15. File be consigned to record after necessary compliance.
